from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Quantifying Uncertainty: The Entropy Formula", [
            "Entropy measures our average uncertainty about an outcome.",
            "We represent this using a probability tree structure.",
            "The formula calculates bits needed to identify words."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in 'Entropy Formula: H(X) = -Σ p(x) log p(x)'. Color: #FFFFFF.
        formula = MathTex(r"H(X) = -\\sum p(x) \\log_2 p(x)", color=WHITE)
        icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg", color=WHITE)
        icon.scale(0.5).next_to(formula, LEFT)
        
        group = VGroup(formula, icon)
        # Applying the fix from Issue 24/37
        self.place_in_area(group, "B1", "C5", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight 'p(x)' representing probability of an event. Color: #32CD32.
        p_x = formula.get_parts_by_tex(r"p(x)")
        self.play(Indicate(p_x, color=GREEN))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#32CD32")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate the log function curve descending. Color: #FFD700.
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 1, 0.2], y_range=[0, 2, 0.5], x_length=3, y_length=2).add_coordinates()
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: -np.log2(x + 1e-9) / 2, x_range=[0.05, 1], color=GOLD)
        
        # Applying the fixes from Issue 25/26/37
        self.place_at_grid(axes, "E3", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(curve, "E3", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        self.wait(2)

        # Position icons
        self.place_at_grid(keyboard_icon, "A2", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(screen_icon, "E2", scale_factor=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(word_label), FadeIn(keyboard_icon), FadeIn(pool_size_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00BFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

outline.topic: Cracking the Code: Information Theory and Entropy in Wordle

sections.title: The Core Concept: What is Information?
sections.content: Introduce Claude Shannon's Information Theory. Define 'Information' not as data, but as the reduction of uncertainty. The more unexpected an event is, the more information it carries.
sections.example: Flipping a coin (high uncertainty/information) vs. looking at a rigged coin that always lands on heads (zero uncertainty/information).

sections.title: Quantifying Uncertainty: The Entropy Formula
sections.content: Explain Entropy (H) as the measure of average uncertainty. Formula: H = -∑ p(x) log2 p(x). Visualize this as a 'Probability Tree' where branches represent possible word outcomes. Entropy represents the average number of bits needed to identify the hidden word.
sections.example: Visualizing a probability tree for a 3-letter word pool; a guess that splits the tree into equal halves provides maximum information (1 bit).

sections.title: Applying Entropy to Wordle
sections.content: Wordle is a game of maximizing information gain. Each guess acts as a 'filter' that eliminates a subset of possible words. An 'optimal' guess minimizes the remaining entropy of the candidate word list.
sections.example: Comparing 'RAISE' vs. 'XYLYL'. 'RAISE' eliminates many words by splitting the search space effectively, while 'XYLYL' provides little information because it rarely narrows down the possibilities.

sections.title: Interactive Demonstration: The Strategy in Motion
sections.content: Show a visual simulation of a Wordle game state. As guesses are entered, show the 'candidate pool' shrinking. Use color-coded entropy bars to demonstrate how selecting the word with the highest information gain drastically reduces the number of remaining options.
sections.example: A digital 'Detective Fox' character choosing 'SLATE'—the bar chart shows the word pool collapsing from 2,300 words down to ~60 in a single turn.

sections.title: Conclusion: Beyond Games
sections.content: Summarize that entropy isn't just for games; it's the foundation for compression algorithms (ZIP files), machine learning decision trees, and data transmission efficiency.
sections.example: How your smartphone keyboard 'guesses' your next word using similar probability-based entropy calculations.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The bits (0 and 1) are placed in the same grid row as the text and are too close to the left, causing potential visual interference with the lecture content. Fix: Line 68-69: self.place_at_grid(bit0, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8); self.place_at_grid(bit1, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=68, object=bit0, bit1)
issues.resolution_note: Adjusted bit (coin) positioning to B4 and B5.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The long data stream occupies rows C-D, creating a cluttered look and poor spatial balance by overextending horizontally across the center. Fix: Line 74: self.place_in_area(data_stream, 'C3', 'C6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=74, object=data_stream)
issues.resolution_note: Adjusted data stream area to C3-C6 and scaled down.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The current positioning fails to utilize the upper-right grid space (A-rows), leading to a 'heavy' middle-row layout. Fix: Line 61: self.place_at_grid(info_text, 'A2', scale_factor=0.9) (line=61, object=info_text)
issues.resolution_note: Moved info_text to A2 and adjusted scale.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The entropy formula is positioned too high and centrally, encroaching on the title area and causing potential clipping. Fix: Line 56: self.place_in_area(formula, 'B1', 'C5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=56, object=formula)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed formula positioning to prevent encroachment, using B1-C5.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The axes object overlaps with the formula at D3, causing visual clutter. Fix: Line 70: self.place_at_grid(axes, 'E3', scale_factor=0.7) (line=70, object=axes)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed axes positioning to E3 to avoid overlap.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The curve is improperly aligned with the axes at D3, creating a disconnected visual hierarchy. Fix: Line 71: self.place_at_grid(curve, 'E3', scale_factor=0.7) (line=71, object=curve)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed curve positioning to E3.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The Wordle grid is centered awkwardly at B2, competing with the vertical space needed for text flow and future animations. Fix: Line 57: self.place_in_area(grid, 'A2', 'B5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=57, object=grid)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed grid placement to A3-C6 per critic instruction.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The 'Entropy Decreasing' label is positioned too low at E3, causing it to appear disconnected from the context and potentially cluttered if more items are added. Fix: Line 74: self.place_at_grid(entropy_text, 'C3', scale_factor=0.7) (line=74, object=entropy_text)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed entropy_text position to C3 per critic instruction.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Visual imbalance: The right-side grid area is significantly underutilized, leaving the left side crowded by lecture text. Fix: Line 57: self.place_in_area(grid, 'A3', 'C6', scale_factor=1.0) (line=57, object=grid)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed grid placement imbalance to A3-C6 per critic instruction.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: Pool size text and the updated value share the same grid position C2, causing content overlap and visual clutter during the update. Fix: Line 74: self.place_at_grid(new_pool_size, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8) (line=74, object=new_pool_size)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed overlapping new_pool_size label by updating its position to grid 'C3'.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The entropy_bar is currently placed at D3, which is too far from the lecture text on the left, leading to inefficient grid space utilization. Fix: Line 60: self.place_in_area(entropy_bar, 'C2', 'C5', scale_factor=0.7) (line=60, object=entropy_bar)
issues.resolution_note: Optimized entropy_bar grid utilization by using place_in_area to set it across C2-C5.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: Word label at B2 is positioned too close to the upper lecture section, risking visual congestion if the font scales up. Fix: Line 58: self.place_at_grid(word_label, 'B1', scale_factor=0.8) (line=58, object=word_label)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed congestion for word_label by moving it to 'B1'.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The dot icon is too close to the lecture text, causing potential visual clutter when animating. Fix: Line 70: self.place_at_grid(dot_icon, 'B5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=70, object=dot_icon)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: Text labels 'Weather', 'Stocks', 'DNA' are horizontally squashed and overlapping with the grid boundary. Fix: Line 71: self.place_in_area(labels_group, 'B6', 'C6', scale_factor=0.5) (line=71, object=text_labels)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The grid 'D1-E6' consumes too much vertical space, competing with the lecture text area. Fix: Line 72: self.place_in_area(grid_visual, 'D3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=72, object=grid_visual)
